rationale: Constellation shows 10/20/30mm graphite all hold hotspot ~325K (nearly thickness-independent over that range), suggesting the plate is not conduction-limited in that regime. Testing far thinner graphite to find where hotspot starts rising, since graphite has the lowest density (1800) of the well-conducting materials and thinner graphite would be the lightest possible design if thermally sufficient.
Same reasoning as 1mm graphite: probing the thin-plate regime below the 10mm point already on record (18 kg/m2, 325K) to see how hotspot responds to reduced thickness.
Interpolation point between 1mm and 10mm graphite to map the hotspot-vs-thickness curve before committing transports.
